:::{#exm-quasipoisson}
#### Quasipoisson standard errors

Suppose a Poisson regression model with an intercept and $p = 2$ covariates
is fit to $n = 50$ observations,
the Pearson $\chi^2$ statistic is $94$,
and the Poisson regression standard error of $\eb_1$ is $0.10$.
By @eq-quasipoisson-theta:

$$
\ba
\eth
&= \frac{94}{50 - (2 + 1)}
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= \frac{94}{47}
&& \text{(subtract)} \\
&= 2
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

so the quasipoisson standard error of $\eb_1$ is

$$
\ba
\sqrt{\eth} \cdot 0.10
&= \sqrt{2} \cdot 0.10
&& \text{(scale the Poisson standard error)} \\
&\approx 0.141
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

The point estimate $\eb_1$ does not change,
but its 95% confidence interval becomes $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41$ times as wide.
If $\eth$ had been close to $1$,
the quasipoisson and Poisson standard errors would nearly agree.

:::
